title: Editorial Policy — Sephiria Guide
description: Editorial policy for Sephiria guide pages: sources, updates, corrections, and what we will not invent.
body:
sephiria-guide.com publishes short English answers to real Sephiria search questions. It is an unofficial fan site, is not affiliated with Team Horay, and is written and maintained by one person. This page explains what the guide pages cover, where their claims come from, how corrections are handled, and how advertising works.

Scope

  • The main body of the site is Sephiria guide pages: beginner route, builds, weapons, Destiny Inscription, Wishing Fountain, Hard Mode, Artifacts and Tablets, bosses, co-op and multiplayer setup, secret rooms, costumes, and the scythe clarification.
  • Each page answers one clear player question, or a tightly related cluster of questions, and links to the page that covers the neighbouring task.
  • A page is added when a question keeps appearing in search and the existing public answers are incomplete, contradictory or written for an earlier build. Thin pages are not added just to cover a keyword.
  • A separate Football Manager 27 section on the same domain follows the same rules but is kept apart from the Sephiria pages.
  • The site does not cover cheats, mods, saves, account issues or anything that requires extracted game files.

Sourcing standard

Guide claims come from public material and, where useful, from first-hand play:

  • Official sources first. The Steam store listing, official news and patch notes decide questions of fact when they conflict with a guide, because the developer's own text describes the build that shipped.
  • Public community records second. Steam discussions, achievement lists and dated community guides are used for routes, unlock conditions and player experience. They are cited with a link so a reader can re-check them.
  • Videos for shapes, not numbers. Clear videos are useful for the order of a route or for what a fight looks like. Exact values are not taken from a montage, because the recording may predate a patch.
  • Two independent sources for contested claims. When sources disagree and the game cannot settle it quickly, both versions are shown instead of one being chosen silently.

Community-reported figures are always labelled, and the page tells the reader to confirm them in-game. Fountain capacity, rarity costs and stage thresholds are the recurring examples: they have changed between builds, so a reported number is presented as a report rather than as a fact. Nothing is inferred from datamining, unreleased builds or leaked files, and no item name, rate or mechanic is invented to fill a gap. When a page cannot confirm something, it says so in a dedicated section.

Versions and dates

Sephiria changes between patches, so the pages that depend on a specific build say which one they describe. Page headers that carry a check date update it when the page changes, and version notes name the public build and any beta branch separately — the 1.1 workshop beta is tracked apart from the public branch because anything in a beta can change before release. Early Access-era numbers and outdated menu paths are marked as legacy rather than deleted, since readers still arrive from old links and need to know why the advice differs.

Updates and corrections

Pages are revised when a patch moves an unlock, when a cited source turns out to be wrong, or when a reader sends a fix that can be reproduced. A wrong claim is corrected on the page rather than left standing; where an outdated path is worth keeping for readers arriving from old links, it is labelled as legacy. Corrections that cannot be verified keep the original hedge instead of being replaced by an unconfirmed claim. When a correction changes the recommendation on a build page, the reason is stated on the page so a returning reader can see what changed.

How to report an error

Email jeromell@be-winner.com or use the contact page. A useful report includes the page URL, the sentence that is wrong, what you see in the current build, and a source that can be re-checked. Reports are handled by one person on a best-effort basis; there is no ticket queue and no promised turnaround. If a fix is confirmed, the page is edited and dated.

Advertising and independence

Guide pages carry no sponsored sections, no paid placements and no paid links. Advertising is served by Google AdSense (publisher ca-pub-8359621843582672) and is kept out of the guide content: the units sit in fixed positions in the article flow, one after the opening paragraph and one before the related-guides block, and they are not inserted into the middle of an answer. Legal pages such as this one, the privacy policy and the contact page carry no ad units.

Ad revenue does not decide what gets written, which build gets recommended, or how a source is described. If the advertising setup changes, this page will say so. Google's handling of ad data is described in the privacy policy and named in ads.txt.

What this site will not do

  • Publish a number as verified when it is a community report.
  • Name an item, upgrade or route that cannot be found in the current client or a cited public source.
  • Present one player's clear as a guaranteed result for other players.
  • Hide a disagreement between sources to make a page read more cleanly.
